32030-selections-from-ancient-irish-poet.title: Selections From Ancient Irish Poetry
32030-selections-from-ancient-irish-poet.creator: Unknown
32030-selections-from-ancient-irish-poet.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Once when Bran, son of Feval, was with his warriors in his  royal fort, they suddenly saw a woman in strange raiment  upon the floor of the house. No one knew whence she had come  or how she had entered, for the ramparts were closed. Then  she sang these quatrains to Bran while all the host were  listening.

66091-eunice-and-cricket.title: Eunice And Cricket
66091-eunice-and-cricket.creator: Elizabeth Westyn Timlow
66091-eunice-and-cricket.description: A book by Elizabeth Westyn Timlow. “Stand still as a mice, Helen,” immediately admonished the small girl in the dark red coat, giving a great pinch to the little golden-haired, brown-clad lassie who stood beside her, by way of emphasising her older sister’s words. “Stand still as a mice, Johnnie-goat,” giving the third member of the group a tickle on the back that made him drop his curved horns for more.

arxiv-1904-02185.title: Dust-acoustic envelope solitons in super-thermal plasmas Journal: “Contributions to Plasma Physics"
arxiv-1904-02185.creator: A. A. Noman ∗,1 , N. A. Chowdhury ∗∗,1 , A. Mannan 1,2 , and A. A. Mamun 1
arxiv-1904-02185.description: Abstract The modulational instability (MI) of the dust-acoustic waves (DAWs) in an electron-positron-ion-dust plasma (containing super-thermal electrons, positrons and ions along with negatively charged adiabatic dust grains) is investigated by the analysis of the nonlinear Schrödinger equation (NLSE). To derive the NLSE, the reductive perturbation method has been employed. Two different parametric regions for stable and unstable DAWs are observed.

arxiv-2201-08566.title: Dynamic phase transition theory
arxiv-2201-08566.creator: Qi-Jun Ye, Xin-Zheng Li
arxiv-2201-08566.description: Abstract Thermodynamic conventions suffer from describing dynamical distinctions, especially when the structural and energetic changes induced by rare events are insignificant. By using the ensemble theory in the trajectory space, we present a statistical approach to address this problem. Rather than spatial particle-particle interaction which dominates thermodynamics, the temporal correlation of events dominates the dynamics.

arxiv-2206-08455.title: Local overlap reduction procedure for dynamic ensemble selection
arxiv-2206-08455.creator: Mariana A. Souza 1 , Robert Sabourin 1 , George D. C. Cavalcanti 2 and Rafael M. O. Cruz 1
arxiv-2206-08455.description: Abstract Class imbalance is a characteristic known for making learning more challenging for classification models as they may end up biased towards the majority class. A promising approach among the ensemble-based methods in the context of imbalance learning is Dynamic Selection (DS).

arxiv-2303-12269.title: A Cycle-Accurate Soft Error Vulnerability Analysis Framework for FPGA-based Designs
arxiv-2303-12269.creator: Eduardo Rhod, Behnam Ghavami, Zhenman Fang, Lesley Shannon
arxiv-2303-12269.description: Abstract Many aerospace and automotive applications use FPGAs in their designs due to their low power and reconfigurability requirements. Meanwhile, such applications also pose a high standard on system reliability, which makes the early-stage reliability analysis for FPGA-based designs very critical.

arxiv-2309-14618.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Ivan Geffner, Joseph Y. Halpern. We consider k k -resilient sequential equilibria , strategy profiles where no player in a coalition of at most k k players believes that it can increase its utility by deviating, regardless of its local state. We prove that all k k -resilient sequential equilibria that can be implemented with a trusted mediator can also be implemented without the mediator in a synchronous system of n n players if n > 3 ​ k n>3k .

arxiv-2310-17099.description: Abstract The known lower bound for the the classical Ramsey number R ⁡ ( 5 , 6 ) R(5,6) is improved from 58 58 to 59 59 . The method used to construct the graph is a simple variant of computational methods that have been previously used to construct Ramsey graphs.

arxiv-2502-12639.title: Effect of laser field and magnetic flux on scattering in graphene quantum dots
arxiv-2502-12639.creator: Mohammed El Azar, Ahmed Bouhlal, Hocine Bahlouli, Ahmed Jellal
arxiv-2502-12639.description: Abstract We show how Dirac electrons interact with a graphene quantum dots (GQDs) when exposed to both a magnetic flux and circularly polarized light. After obtaining the solutions of the energy spectrum, we compute the scattering coefficients. These allow us to show how efficiently the electrons diffuse and how their probability density is distributed in space.

arxiv-2504-08928.title: Observability of Acausal and Uncorrelated Optical-Quasar Pairs for Quantum-Mechanical Experiments
arxiv-2504-08928.creator: Eric Steinbring
arxiv-2504-08928.description: Abstract Viewing high-redshift sources at near-opposite directions on the sky can assure, by light-travel-time arguments, acausality between their emitted photons. One utility would be true random-number generation, by sensing these via two independent telescopes that each flip a switch based on those latest-arrived colours; for example, to autonomously control a quantum-mechanical (QM) experiment.

pmc-10670542.title: Preparing for Death While Investing in Life: A Narrative Inquiry and Case Report of Home-Based Paediatric Palliative, End-of-Life, and After-Death Care
pmc-10670542.creator: Michelle Noyes, Angela Delaney, Meagan Lang, Mellissa Maybury, Susan Moloney, Natalie Bradford
pmc-10670542.description: Paediatric palliative care is pivotal for addressing the complex needs of children with incurable diseases and their families. While home-based care offers a familiar and supportive environment, delivering comprehensive services in this context is challenging. The existing literature on home-based palliative care lacks detailed guidance for its organization and implementation.

pmc-11306130.title: A cross-sectional study of non-suicidal self-injury in adolescent depression: association with demographic characteristics and physiological indicators
pmc-11306130.creator: Yangliuqing He, Yuhan Wei, Yiming Wang, Fenrong Liang, Tianpei Ma
pmc-11306130.description: IntroductionNon-suicidal self-injury (NSSI) is a prevalent concern among adolescents with depression, yet its relationship with demographic characteristics and physiological indicators remains underexplored. This study aimed to investigate these relationships among inpatient adolescents aged 13 to 18 at a hospital affiliated with Guizhou Medical University.MethodsA cross-sectional study was conducted involving 222 adolescent inpatients diagnosed with depression.

pmc-11313604.title: Evaluation of Postoperative Pain When Adding a Tibial Nerve Block to the Femoral Nerve Block for Total Knee Arthroplasty
pmc-11313604.creator: Alejandra Mira-Puerto, Pedro Romero-Aroca, Alfredo Rodríguez-Gangoso, Albert Ferrando-de Jorge, Mireia Duart-Oltra, Pilar Sala-Francino, Mari Carmen Martínez-Segovia, Marc Baget-Bernaldiz
pmc-11313604.description: Background: The aim of this study was to compare the postoperative analgesic efficacy when a tibial nerve block was added to the femoral nerve block for total knee arthroplasty (TKA). Methods: A total of 60 patients were randomly assigned to the experimental group (EG) or the control group (CG) in a 1:1 ratio.

pmc-11341597.creator: Brett A Baxter, Anthony W Baross, Declan J Ryan, Anthony D Kay
pmc-11341597.description: BackgroundEccentric resistance training elicits greater preservation of training-induced muscular adaptations compared with other training modalities, however the detraining profiles of different training dosages remain unknown.AimsTo examine the detraining effects following once- or twice-weekly eccentric-specific resistance training in older adults.MethodsTwenty-one older adults (age = 70.5 ± 6.

pmc-11704154.title: Continuous frusemide infusion versus intermittent bolus therapy in paediatric intensive care: A single centre retrospective study
pmc-11704154.creator: Nutnicha Preeprem, Emily See, Siva P Namachivayam, Ben Gelbart
pmc-11704154.description: ObjectiveFrusemide is a common diuretic administered to critically ill children intravenously, by either continuous infusion (CI) or intermittent bolus (IB). We aim to describe the characteristics of children who receive intravenous frusemide, patterns of use, and incidence of acute kidney injury (AKI), and to investigate factors associated with commencing CI.DesignRetrospective observational study.

pmc-12624866.title: Histone lactylation exacerbates acute lung injury in septic mice by promoting ferroptosis in pulmonary microvascular endothelial cells
pmc-12624866.creator: Pu Fang, Shuai Li, Zong-Qing Lu, Dun-Lin Xia, Meng-Meng Xu, Jing-Jing Pan, Lin Fu, Geng-Yun Sun, Qing-Hai You
pmc-12624866.description: BackgroundCirculating lactate is associated with poor prognosis in sepsis-induced acute lung injury (S-ALI). However, it remains unclear whether microvascular dysfunction, a hallmark of S-ALI, is related to circulating lactate levels and what the underlying mechanisms are. The aim of this study was to investigate the role and mechanisms of lactate in pulmonary microvascular dysfunction in S-ALI.

pmc-12655840.title: In Vitro Antibacterial Efficacy of a New TiO2-Cu-Coated Titanium Surface for Biomedical Applications
pmc-12655840.creator: Mahalakshmi Pandian, Sacha Cavelier, Simone Guttau, Silvia Cometta, Joseph Fernando, Philipp Kobbe, Dietmar W. Hutmacher
pmc-12655840.description: Despite advancements in surgical care, the management of surgical site infections (SSIs) associated with fracture-fixation devices is still a challenge after implant fixation, especially in open fractures. Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus) is a common pathogen of SSIs and contaminates by penetrating the trauma itself (preoperatively) or during insertion of the fixation device (intraoperatively).

pmc-13115116.title: Hemodialysis Tends to Improve Thyroid Function by Restoring Hormone Levels in ESRD Patients Compared to Non-Dialysis Kidney Disease Patients: A Case–Control Study
pmc-13115116.creator: Hasibul Islam, Shahad Saif Khandker, Anwara Khatun, Ehsan Suez, Alif Hasan Pranto, Dewan Zubaer Islam, Rahima Begum, Md. Nizam Uddin, Md. Ashraful Hasan, Md. Shah Alam, A. N. M. Mamun-Or-Rashid
pmc-13115116.description: Background: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) represents an escalating global health burden, fundamentally altering morbidity and mortality trajectories across the world, particularly as it advances into end-stage renal disease (ESRD). Beyond the primary decline in renal filtration and excretion, a wide spectrum of endocrine and metabolic derangements frequently accompanies kidney failure, with thyroid dysfunction emerging as a critical complication.

pmc-13200304.title: Mpox outbreak preparedness and response capacity in Nigeria’s Federal Capital Territory: a mixed-methods study
pmc-13200304.creator: Tina Aribi, Charles Chibuisi Ehiemere, Ishaku Adamu Akyala, Istifanus Haruna Nkene, Idowu Olapemi Makinde, Rabi Usman, Temitope Babalola Oluwapemi, Chukwuma John Nosike
pmc-13200304.description: BackgroundMpox has re-emerged globally as a public health threat, with implications for low-resource settings where surveillance and response systems remain fragile. Nigeria’s Federal Capital Territory (FCT) hosts large mobile populations and international institutions, heightening outbreak vulnerability. Evidence on sub-national preparedness capacity is limited. This study assessed Mpox awareness, preparedness, and institutional response capabilities across the FCT using a mixed-methods approach.

pmc-13642553.title: Hybrid Metalens–Compressive Sensing Imaging System for Ultra‐Low‐Power Edge Detection
pmc-13642553.creator: Sejin Yoon, Hasung Kim, Hyunkeun Lee, Trevon Badloe
pmc-13642553.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Low‐power edge detection is essential for next‐generation vision systems that require real‐time on‐device processing of optical information. Conventional imagers rely on power‐intensive digital postprocessing for edge detection, creating a data bottleneck between the image sensor and signal processor. We propose a system‐level hybrid optoelectronic edge imaging framework that combines an analog optical computing metalens with a compressive sensing CMOS image sensor (CS‐CIS).
